conclusion: Four contained source defects were repaired and regression/compatibility evidence collected. The inspected SDK usage is compatible with the pinned contracts; no blanket claim of zero defects, complete feature parity or production readiness is justified. Larger shutdown/End findings remain open.

fixed_findings.title: P2 could not retry a failed native SDK close
fixed_findings.before: The runtime kept its failed close task forever. An SDK close failure left the resource owned, but every later public aclose only rethrew that old failure; its own test repaired a private field.
fixed_findings.after: Pending and successful close attempts remain shared. A definitively failed/cancelled attempt permits one later public retry. Admission remains fenced, independent work drains, and observer cancellation does not abandon actual cleanup.
fixed_findings.validation: Genuine pinned-SDK regression failed before the fix; 18 native SDK tests passed after, including concurrent retries and a cancelled close waiter.

fixed_findings.title: P3 could remain stuck after definite pre-acceptance capacity rejection
fixed_findings.before: The attempted flag was set before submit. A definite capacity rejection could leave all future calls inspecting work that had never been accepted.
fixed_findings.after: Only initial-submit capacity restores explicit retry of the same frozen request. Unknown acceptance and any post-acceptance runner failure remain lookup-only; no new work identity or hidden retry is introduced.
fixed_findings.validation: 18 policy tests and 3 genuine SDK tests pass. New negatives distinguish unknown submit ACK and capacity after acceptance. The authority/specialist in this focused schedule are in-memory fixtures, not PostgreSQL.

fixed_findings.title: Older P1 diagnostic failures could replace operation truth
fixed_findings.before: A logger could raise after finish_success, causing a successful public worker call to report failure. A hostile diagnostic code getter could replace the original exception. Eight older logging helpers shared the escape pattern.
fixed_findings.after: Ordinary telemetry exceptions are contained in those helpers; managed and legacy inquiry error-code extraction is protected. Fatal BaseException control flow remains unsuppressed. No schema, transaction, consent or retry rule changed.
fixed_findings.validation: Four regression methods were observed failing before their corresponding fixes. All 19 inquiry-worker tests pass, including eight logger outage cases, fatal propagation and preserved public results/errors.

fixed_findings.title: Provider instructions invented running work from a noncurrent result
fixed_findings.before: The prompt told the model that no_delivery, not_applicable and unavailable all meant the policy check was still running. Those states can instead reflect a completed stale result or a failed read.
fixed_findings.after: The prompt asks for a neutral no-current-answer response and explicitly says those states do not establish whether work is running. Current-result facts and exact action authority remain separate.
fixed_findings.validation: Existing 13 offline provider-mode tests pass. This verifies composition/wire contracts, not whether a live model consistently follows the revised instruction; actual provider/media qualification was not rerun.

remaining_priority_findings.title: Whole-showcase shutdown still closes Parent dependencies before gateway dispatch
remaining_priority_findings.detail: The launcher awaits Parent cleanup before stopping the gateway child. Parent can close origin endpoints while gateway dispatch still consumes attempts. The previous audit records permanent pending-input exhaustion. This needs an explicit stop-dispatch/drain protocol and actual persisted/process evidence, not a tutorial shutdown hook.

remaining_priority_findings.confidence: medium; previously reasoned race, not newly reproduced
remaining_priority_findings.title: Room End can race the last accepted input
remaining_priority_findings.detail: Room cleanup stops the worker before _close_g closes the gateway room binding. The previous audit identifies a stranding window for the last input. A valid repair must fence new admission while preserving and reconciling the original accepted operation; fresh PostgreSQL/process/media proof is required.

remaining_priority_findings.title: Joined cleanup budgets and repeated observation still need reconciliation
remaining_priority_findings.detail: The recorded two-second scripted room, five-second Parent and up-to-eight-second provider cleanup windows do not form a consistent end-to-end drain budget. The P2 retry repair fixes its owned API, not the larger launcher/Parent shutdown design.

remaining_priority_findings.title: Persisted v5 retry pacing does not cover every post-reservation outage
remaining_priority_findings.detail: Do not describe all dependency outages as covered by the current persisted backoff. Preserve dispatch uncertainty and original effects when designing the next slice.

findings.title: A failed native runtime close permanently blocked public cleanup retry
findings.mechanism: _start_owned_close previously returned whenever _close_task existed, including a definitively failed task. If session.aclose raised once, _close_owned drained independent owners and raised NativeCleanupIncomplete, but every later public aclose only observed the cached failure. The application could not retry the retained SDK resource through the public lifecycle API.

evidence.claim: Owned-close task sharing and failed-task retry decision.
Public close fences admission and shields the actual owned close task.
SDK close failure is sanitized while independent cleanup continues.
Existing close-failure regression formerly required private _close_task=None repair; now exercises public retry.

reproducible_schedule: Start the genuine pinned AgentSession with synthetic local STT/LLM/TTS and hold an intake plus observer.
Inject one session.aclose exception; release independent work and observe sanitized NativeCleanupIncomplete with sdk_closed false.
Restore the SDK close implementation and call public runtime.aclose. Before the fix the SDK close is never entered; a bounded regression fails waiting for that entry.

After the fix, hold the new SDK close, start a second public close waiter, cancel the first waiter, and verify only one actual retry remains owned. Release it and observe sdk_closed true and successful subsequent close.
findings.test_weakness_corrected: The old assertion proved independent drains and safe diagnostics but repaired a private field in teardown, masking lack of public retry. The replacement checks retry entry, concurrent sharing, continued admission fencing, cancellation of one waiter without cancellation of the actual owner, eventual SDK closure and reuse of successful close.
findings.change: Only a definitively failed/cancelled cached task may be replaced. Pending and successful close tasks remain shared; the new task still uses eager_start=False and public waiters remain shielded.
findings.limitations: The regression injects a transient exception before genuine SDK closure and proves retry ownership. It does not certify recovery from every possible internal SDK failure or browser transport failure.

findings.title: A valid remote contract rejection is reported by the runner as invalid_result
findings.evidence: The transport deliberately represents a valid delegation.error envelope as ContractError(code), including unauthorized/capacity. The runner catches ContractError from invoke_observed and always converts it to invalid_result. That conflates a correctly framed remote rejection with malformed or mismatched result bytes.
findings.safety: The path fails closed; it does not complete a result or authorize reinvocation. This is an operator-diagnosis/metric issue, not evidence of duplicate external execution.

intentional_differences.title: Native conversational TaskGroup is not the durable P1 execution queue
intentional_differences.explanation: The baseline intentionally compares one tool and real SDK AgentTask/TaskGroup within a single session. Durable acceptance/issuance/results are supplied by the separate P1-backed facade. No SDK task, generic result annotation or model statement grants durable invocation or action authority.

intentional_differences.title: The implementation correctly uses the pinned Python task API rather than incompatible Academy examples
intentional_differences.explanation: Installed 1.8.11 takes task factories plus id/description, awaits the TaskGroup and exposes task_results. It does not accept the Academy's shown output_type, group.run(session) or summarize_between_tasks forms. P3 also explicitly validates the returned runtime PolicyResult because AgentTask.complete merely stores its Python value/exception.

intentional_differences.title: SDK waiter cancellation and durable business cancellation are intentionally separate
intentional_differences.explanation: CANCELLABLE allows the conversational waiter to stop. A shielded actual runner and its public owner's pending count remain retained; no automatic P1 cancellation is inferred. The focused actual-SDK test proves useful held-work continuation using scripted model and fake durable ports, not live media or provider behavior.

intentional_differences.title: Only newly created issuance followed by the exact fresh running grant permits HTTP invocation
intentional_differences.explanation: Issue ACK ambiguity reconciles the original command and returns a view; created=false does not invoke. A created grant is compared against a fresh running observation, cancellation and expiry before transport. Verified result truth is then recorded via public P1 completion; current case applicability is a separate read.

intentional_differences.title: Cross-principal result/cancel grants are an explicit trust-policy choice
intentional_differences.explanation: Historical P3-A9 is not an unauthenticated bypass: current scope/capability credentials are required. A distinct result principal and distinct cancel principal are deliberately tested. Binding observation/control exclusively to the starting principal would change this delegated-operations policy and needs an explicit design decision.

intentional_differences.title: Observer-owned telemetry resources do not extend server ownership
intentional_differences.explanation: Notifications are bounded/dropped rather than becoming an unbounded telemetry queue. The documented observer contract makes its external resources application-owned; successful server close is not a claim that arbitrary observer-created exporter I/O has closed.

intentional_differences.title: Late verified result truth, delivery receipt and exact action permission remain separate
intentional_differences.explanation: A stored eligible-at-commit result is historical P1 time/lease/cancel truth, not an evergreen action permit. Delivery uses immutable receiver intent and possible-send lookup semantics. Exact human confirmation and current atomic public P1 action guards remain separate from model tools.
